rationale: Stem asks what the Seneca Falls reformers were most directly doing by modeling their Declaration of Sentiments on the Declaration of Independence; the task is identifying the source's purpose (claiming the founding ideals of liberty and equality for women) => 2.A. Content is the 1848 Seneca Falls convention => 4.11.

Stem asks by what mechanism the Dawes Act reduced Native landholding; the task is identifying a historical development/process (allotment plus sale of 'surplus' land) => 1.A. Content is the 1887 Dawes Severalty Act => 6.2.

Stem asks what a historian must take into account about The Liberator; the task is identifying the source's POV and purpose (an openly immediatist abolitionist journal, not a neutral sample of opinion) => 2.A. Content is 1831 immediatist abolitionism => 4.11.

Stem asks what rock as the 1960s generation's common language shows; the task is identifying a historical development (a generation-wide youth culture crossing regions and campuses) => 1.A. Content is 1960s youth culture => 8.12.
Stem asks which law-year match is correct; straightforward identification of historical developments => 1.A. Content is 1970s federal environmental legislation => 8.13.

Stem asks what creating a permanent EPA signaled; explaining the significance of the development (a lasting federal commitment to policing pollution) => 1.B. Content is 1970 environmental institutionalization => 8.13.

Stem asks what Kellogg's private dismissal of the pact shows; the task is identifying the architect's point of view (doubt that paper promises could stop war) => 2.A. Content is the Kellogg-Briand Pact => 7.11.
